correctness.rationale: The published three-dimensional cube perimeter maximum gives precisely 12 signed-permutation maximizers. Independently reconstructed quadrilateral and hexagon face-perimeter formulas have uniform local deficits 2 sqrt(2) r and 2 sqrt(2) q respectively, hence the square-cusp 2 sqrt(2) max(r,q). The signed ordered-coordinate map has spherical Jacobian ((1+r)^2+1+q^2)^(-3/2), tending to 1/(2 sqrt(2)); multiplying the local square area by 48/(4 pi) yields 3 sqrt(2)/(8 pi). The same dominated-convergence argument proves the uniform-square conditional weak law, whose diagonal split is 1/2 and whose max is Beta(2,1). Face-edge hull reconstruction, local asymptotics, and 3.2 million Gaussian orientations were executed successfully using the attached verifier; finite tests do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The topology-changing maximal central cube section lies on a polygon-type seam. Its nonsmooth two-dimensional orientation deficit is natural geometric structure; the explicit quadratic upper-tail rate and full conditional uniform-square law quantify how often extreme slices occur and why hexagonal and quadrilateral sections contribute equally. An unconditioned combinatorial type probability and global perimeter maximum do not alone reveal this marked rare-shape behavior. The geometric contrast with the separately known extreme-section-area split (unequal rather than one-half) shows the choice of area versus perimeter changes which combinatorial type dominates, so this is not an arbitrary change of threshold or scaling.
